content:
Looking at the fold lines: the octagon is folded along a vertical axis, then a horizontal axis, then a diagonal axis, producing a 45°–67.5°–67.5° triangle whose apex is the **center** of the octagon.

The cut removes the corner at the center apex, with the cut perpendicular to one of the fold edges. Unfolding reverses the three reflections (generating all 8 symmetric copies of the cut):

- Reflecting the small right-triangle cut across the horizontal fold line gives an isosceles triangle.
- Reflecting across the diagonal fold line turns that into a quarter-square wedge.
- Reflecting across the vertical fold line (and rotations) completes four such wedges around the center.

The union of these 8 copies forms a square hole whose sides are parallel/perpendicular to the first two fold lines (vertical and horizontal), i.e., an axis-aligned square hole in the middle of the octagon — not tilted, not octagonal, and not a star.

\boxed{C}
